name: BoingBag 3.9-2
_why_distinguished_by_repeats_the_member: ART-167. Two of the owner's archives carry the top-level directory
the same BoingBag's contributed extras. Measured (44 archives walked,
and `XAD-Update`; the Contribution archive's holds `Contribution` and
the readmes, and no payload member at all.
So the string below is the same one `member` names, and it is written
twice on purpose. `member` says where this package's payload lives;
`distinguished_by` says which archive is this package's. They are not
the same fact, and the same measurement shows it: `AmigaOS-Update` is
carried by `BoingBag39-1.lha` too, so as an identity on its own it
separates nothing — it only settles this pair because the other
claimant of `BoingBag3.9-2` happens to lack it. Folding the two fields
together would encode a coincidence as a rule.
_why_host_placement_block: ART-166, measured in Task 8's real run and confirmed three independent ways (ART's own reader, 7-Zip 26.02, the raw general-purpose flag word 0x0003 with bit 0 set): the `AmigaOS-Update` member named above is a ZIP whose every entry is ZipCrypto-encrypted — 233 of 233 entries in 3.9-1's payload, 147 of 147 in 3.9-2's. The password belongs to the BoingBag's own `Updater`, which the wrapper LHA carries beside the payload and which has to run *on* an Amiga; every established distribution builder (HstWB Installer, AmiKit, AmigaSYS, ClassicWB) installs a BoingBag by running that Updater inside an emulator rather than by decrypting anything, and the owner's recorded decision is that ART will write no bypass.  So the rules below are right and unreachable, and spec §10/§89 says ART must not offer what it cannot do. Declaring the block here — data, not code — is what makes the screen refuse the tick with a translated sentence naming the Updater, instead of accepting it and meeting the reader's own raw English `Password required to decrypt file` after the user already confirmed. **That prediction was wrong, and is corrected here rather than left standing (2026-08-25).** It read: "The day the Amiga-side install round lands, this one key is deleted and nothing else changes." That round landed on 2026-08-21 and both BoingBags installed on the owner's own material through ART's own compose-then-install path - and this key STAYS. The block is about placing the payload's files from the host, which is as impossible as it ever was: the Amiga's own Updater writes them, inside the emulator, after the package's own code decrypts its own payload. Deleting this key would put a live tick back on a screen that still cannot do what the tick promises.
_why_amiga_installer: Measured separately from 3.9-1's rather than copied, the same rule this
file's own top comment follows (2026-08-20, 7-Zip 26.02 against the
owner's BoingBag39-2.lha). It happens to agree, and the agreement is a
reading, not an assumption:
1. `BoingBag3.9-2\C\Updater` is a real entry, 42 676 bytes — a
different build from 3.9-1's 25 588-byte one — so the path relative
to the top-level directory is `C/Updater` here too. This archive
also carries `BoingBag3.9-2\C\Installer`, which 3.9-1 does not;
that is the Installer *engine* the `Install` script needs, not the
thing that installs this package.
2. This package's `Install` script, line 1615, runs
`C/Updater AmigaOS-Update "<target>"` — identical in shape to
One thing 3.9-1 has no counterpart for: line 1632 runs the Updater a
second time, `C/Updater XAD-Update "<target>"`, guarded by
`(if (= #install-xad-update 1) ...)` — a choice the script's own
requester puts to the user. It is NOT declared here. `AmigaInstaller`
describes one run, this round installs what the package is (the AmigaOS
update), and declaring an optional extra as though it were part of the
package would install something the user was never asked about. The day
ART offers that choice, it is a second declaration, not a code path.

Declaring what has not been tried is the §89 mistake from the other

_why_post_install: ART-227, and this one is the whole reason the mechanism exists.
BoingBag 2's `Updater` writes its ROM update as
`Devs/AmigaOS ROM Update.BB39-2` — **321 768 bytes** — and leaves it there,
beside the CD's own 127 956-byte `Devs/AmigaOS ROM Update`, under a name
`SetPatch` does not load. Measured on 2026-08-24 on the tree ART's own run
produced: both files present, the old one still the active one. So a tree that
reports itself BoingBag'd, and answers `Workbench 45.3` when asked, is running
the ROM update it had before. Nothing fails; the newer file is simply never
HstWB Installer does the same move — back the old one aside, copy the new one
over it — which is where this was found. ART does it on the host instead of in
the boot script, for the reasons `core::amigainstall::finish` gives.
**`NSDPatch.cfg` is deliberately left alone.** BoingBag 1 leaves
(the two packages do not even agree on the punctuation), and neither is rotated
here. That file is user-editable configuration; a reference copy beside it is
the right shape, and HstWB reaches the same conclusion by touching neither.
